Name: Feature Store
Use Case: Serve pre-computed features to ML models at training and inference time with consistency
Strengths: Single source of truth for features; reduces training-serving skew; feature reuse across teams
Weaknesses: Complex infrastructure; cold-start for new features; versioning complexity
Alternatives: Feast; Tecton; Hopsworks; Vertex AI Feature Store; SageMaker Feature Store
Gotcha: Training-serving skew is the #1 silent ML bug — if you compute features differently at training vs serving your model degrades silently

Name: Model Registry
Use Case: Version and track ML models with metadata and lineage through their lifecycle
Strengths: Model versioning; reproducibility; approval workflows; A/B testing support
Weaknesses: Adds process overhead; requires team discipline; integration with serving infrastructure
Alternatives: MLflow Model Registry; Weights & Biases; Vertex AI Model Registry; SageMaker Model Registry
Gotcha: A model registry without lineage tracking is just a file store — track data version + code version + hyperparameters

Name: Experiment Tracking
Use Case: Track hyperparameters and metrics and artifacts across ML experiment runs
Strengths: Reproducibility; comparison across runs; team collaboration; audit trail
Weaknesses: Storage costs for artifacts; requires discipline to log everything; tool lock-in
Alternatives: MLflow; Weights & Biases; Neptune; Comet; ClearML
Gotcha: Tracking only metrics without data/code versions makes experiments non-reproducible

Name: Online vs Offline Serving
Use Case: Choose between real-time (online) and batch (offline) model inference
Strengths: Online: low-latency per-request prediction; Offline: high-throughput batch scoring
Weaknesses: Online: infrastructure cost and complexity; Offline: stale predictions
Alternatives: Online: TF Serving; Triton; KServe; vLLM. Offline: Spark; Batch transform
Gotcha: Online serving latency budget must include feature retrieval — a 5ms model with 200ms feature fetch defeats the purpose

Name: Training-Serving Skew
Use Case: Detect and prevent differences between training-time and serving-time feature computation
Strengths: Feature stores eliminate skew; monitoring detects drift; integration tests catch mismatches
Weaknesses: Hard to detect in production; manifests as silent accuracy degradation
Alternatives: Feature Store; data validation (Great Expectations; TFX Data Validation)
Gotcha: Skew can come from: different code paths for feature computation; different library versions; time-dependent features computed at different times

Name: ML Pipeline Orchestration
Use Case: Automate end-to-end ML workflow: data prep → training → evaluation → deployment
Strengths: Reproducible pipelines; scheduled retraining; dependency management; lineage
Weaknesses: Complex setup; debugging distributed pipelines is hard; vendor lock-in
Alternatives: Kubeflow Pipelines; Vertex AI Pipelines; SageMaker Pipelines; Airflow; Dagster; Prefect
Gotcha: Orchestrator choice depends on team size — Airflow for data-eng-heavy teams; Kubeflow for K8s-native teams

Name: Data Validation
Use Case: Validate input data quality before training or serving to catch schema and distribution drift
Strengths: Catches data bugs early; prevents training on corrupted data; monitors production data quality
Weaknesses: False positives if thresholds too tight; requires baseline statistics
Alternatives: Great Expectations; TFX Data Validation; Pandera; Deequ
Gotcha: Data quality issues cause more ML failures than model architecture choices — validate early and often

Name: Model Monitoring
Use Case: Monitor model performance in production for accuracy degradation and data drift
Strengths: Catches model decay; enables automated retraining triggers; compliance audit trail
Weaknesses: Requires ground truth labels (often delayed); false alarms on normal seasonal changes
Gotcha: Ground truth delay means you can't measure accuracy in real-time — use proxy metrics (prediction distribution shift) as early warning

Name: GPU Resource Management
Use Case: Efficiently share GPU resources across training and inference workloads
Strengths: Cost optimization through sharing; queue-based scheduling; priority tiers
Weaknesses: GPU memory fragmentation; scheduling complexity; multi-tenancy isolation
Alternatives: Run:ai; NVIDIA MIG; Kubernetes GPU scheduling; Ray; SkyPilot
Gotcha: GPU utilization in most orgs is 20-30% — time-slicing and MIG can double effective utilization

Name: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
Use Case: Combine LLM generation with relevant document retrieval for grounded and up-to-date responses
Strengths: Reduces hallucination; uses current data without retraining; interpretable via citations
Weaknesses: Retrieval quality is the bottleneck; chunking strategy matters enormously; latency overhead
Alternatives: LangChain; LlamaIndex; Haystack; custom retrieval + LLM
Gotcha: Chunk size and overlap determine RAG quality more than the LLM choice — experiment with 256-1024 token chunks

Name: Vector Database
Use Case: Store and query high-dimensional embeddings for similarity search at scale
Strengths: Sub-millisecond similarity search; scales to billions of vectors; integrates with ML pipelines
Weaknesses: Index building is expensive; approximate results (not exact); operational complexity
Alternatives: Pinecone; Weaviate; Qdrant; Milvus; Chroma; pgvector
Gotcha: ANN (approximate nearest neighbor) means you trade recall for speed — tune nprobe/ef parameters based on your accuracy requirements

Name: LLM Fine-Tuning
Use Case: Adapt a pre-trained large language model to domain-specific tasks
Strengths: Better domain performance than prompting alone; smaller model can match larger base model
Weaknesses: Expensive compute; catastrophic forgetting risk; needs curated training data
Alternatives: Full fine-tuning; LoRA; QLoRA; PEFT; Prefix tuning
Gotcha: LoRA reduces trainable parameters by 10000x with minimal quality loss — try it before full fine-tuning
